slots.practicalActivity: Write a precise one-paragraph rebuttal to the lesson's colleague argument ('just use a brighter lamp'), explicitly using the threshold-frequency photoelectric behavior to explain why no amount of brightness below the threshold frequency produces a single photoelectron.
slots.deliverable: A written rebuttal paragraph that cites the threshold-frequency mechanism specifically, not just 'classical physics is wrong.'

slots.practicalActivity: Write a precise rebuttal to the claim that an electron 'splits into two half-electrons' through the double slit, using both (a) each particle landing as one localized dot and (b) interference vanishing the instant which-path information exists, then restate the correct amplitude-based description in your own words.
slots.deliverable: A written rebuttal addressing both cited facts, plus a correct one-paragraph restatement of the amplitude/interference picture.

slots.practicalActivity: Using |ψ⟩=0.6|0⟩+0.8|1⟩, work through the check-yourself scenario in writing: state the probability that a measurement yielding outcome 1 was going to occur (postulate 3), then state the qubit's exact post-measurement state (postulate 4), and explain why a second immediate measurement is now deterministic.
slots.deliverable: A written answer citing postulate 3 for the probability and postulate 4 for the collapsed state, plus the deterministic-second-measurement explanation.

lessons.title: Quantum Mechanics for Computing, Not Physics Majors

slots.practicalActivity: Write a point-by-point rebuttal to a classmate's claim that 'skipping the hydrogen atom means this isn't real QM,' explicitly distinguishing the five postulates (the theory) from the hydrogen atom and perturbation theory (an application), and tying the rebuttal to the 'gates are unitary operators' argument.
slots.deliverable: A written rebuttal that names the postulate-vs-application distinction explicitly and uses the unitary-operators argument to justify the course's scope.

slots.practicalActivity: Answer the lab's own closing question in full: describe, citing postulates 1-4 by number, what happens from start to finish when a single qubit prepared in superposition is measured once, then explain in 1-2 sentences why this sequence is what 'reading out a quantum computation' means.
slots.deliverable: A written, postulate-numbered walkthrough of state/outcome/probability/collapse for one measurement, plus the 1-2 sentence closing explanation.

lessons.title: The Qubit as a Quantum State

slots.practicalActivity: Check whether ψ=0.5|0⟩+0.5|1⟩ is a valid quantum state using the normalization condition, show the arithmetic, and compute the correct amplitude that should replace both 0.5s to make it a valid, equally-weighted state.
slots.deliverable: The normalization check showing ψ fails, plus the corrected amplitude value (1/sqrt(2)) that does satisfy normalization.

slots.practicalActivity: Compute ⟨1|+⟩ for |+⟩=(|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2 by hand using the bra-ket inner product definition, then state what the squared magnitude of your answer represents physically.
slots.deliverable: The computed ⟨1|+⟩ value and its squared magnitude, with a written statement of the probability it represents.

slots.practicalActivity: Using |0⟩=(|+⟩+|−⟩)/√2, express the state |ψ⟩=|0⟩ entirely in terms of |+⟩ and |−⟩, and write a short explanation of why this is a legitimate alternative description of the same physical state rather than a different state.
slots.deliverable: The |+⟩/|−⟩ expression for |0⟩ and a written explanation of why it describes the same physical state.

slots.practicalActivity: Check whether |ψ⟩=0.5|0⟩+(√0.75)|1⟩ is normalized by computing |a|²+|b|² by hand, then determine whether multiplying this entire state by −1 changes anything physically observable, explaining your reasoning using the global-phase concept.
slots.deliverable: The normalization calculation (showing it equals 1) and a written explanation of why multiplying by −1 is an unobservable global phase.

slots.practicalActivity: Work the lab's own closing problem: determine whether ψ=0.7|0⟩+0.7|1⟩ is a valid normalized state, and if not, find the correct amplitude that should replace 0.7 on both terms to make it valid.
slots.deliverable: The normalization check showing 0.7/0.7 fails, plus the corrected amplitude (1/sqrt(2)) with verification that it sums to 1.

slots.practicalActivity: Write out, in your own words, the specific experiment (Hadamard applied twice to |0⟩) you'd point a skeptical classmate to in order to disprove 'superposition is secretly 0 or 1,' explicitly naming what a classical hidden-value model would predict instead and why H·H=I rules that out.
slots.deliverable: A written explanation naming the H·H=I experiment, the classical prediction it would need to match, and why the deterministic return to |0⟩ rules out hidden values.

slots.practicalActivity: For |ψ⟩=0.6|0⟩+0.8|1⟩ run through a quantum circuit 1000 times, compute by hand roughly how many of the 1000 runs would read out 1, and write a short explanation of why you can't shortcut this by measuring once and trusting that single result to represent the full state.
slots.deliverable: The computed expected count of about 640 runs reading 1, plus a written explanation of why a single measurement can't reveal the full amplitude information.

slots.practicalActivity: A qubit starts in |+⟩ and is measured in the computational basis, yielding outcome 0. Write out exactly what the qubit's state is immediately afterward, what a second immediate measurement would give, and explain specifically why you cannot undo the measurement to recover the original |+⟩.
slots.deliverable: A written three-part answer: post-measurement state, second-measurement prediction, and the irreversibility explanation.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a paragraph explaining why it is correct that |0⟩ is simultaneously a definite state in the computational basis and an exact 50/50 superposition in the X-basis, without contradiction, concluding with whether 'superposition' is a property of a state alone or relative to a chosen basis.
slots.deliverable: A written paragraph resolving the apparent contradiction and a clear concluding statement on the basis-relativity of superposition.

slots.practicalActivity: Work the lab's own closing scenario in full: |ψ⟩=√(1/3)|0⟩+√(2/3)|1⟩ is measured in the computational basis and yields 0. State the probability that outcome had, describe the qubit's exact post-measurement state, then walk through step by step what happens if you apply a Hadamard gate to that post-measurement state and measure again.
slots.deliverable: The stated probability (1/3), the exact post-measurement state (|0⟩), and a step-by-step trace of the Hadamard-then-measure sequence that follows.

slots.practicalActivity: Take the state (|00⟩+|01⟩)/√2 and run the full product-state factoring test: set up the ansatz, match coefficients, and determine whether it factors (giving the specific a,b,c,d) or is entangled (showing the contradiction).
slots.deliverable: The full coefficient-matching work and a final verdict (product state, with specific a,b,c,d values) for this state.

slots.practicalActivity: Starting from |00⟩, apply CNOT first (qubit 1 control, qubit 2 target) and only then apply Hadamard to qubit 1, tracking the amplitudes through both steps by hand, and determine whether you still end up with |Φ+⟩ or something different.
slots.deliverable: The amplitude trace through both gate orderings and a written conclusion on whether the result still equals |Φ+⟩, explaining why gate order matters here.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a response to a colleague who claims single-basis |Φ+⟩ statistics prove there's 'no real evidence' entanglement is special: name the specific additional experiment (multi-basis/CHSH measurement) they'd need to run and the specific pattern of results that would prove them wrong.
slots.deliverable: A written response naming the multi-basis CHSH experiment and the |S|>2 result that would disprove the local-hidden-variable explanation.

slots.practicalActivity: An experimenter measures |S|=1.9 on a pair claimed to be entangled. Write a conclusion about whether this pair is genuinely entangled per the CHSH test, and explain why a device-independent QKD protocol would treat this as a red flag rather than accepting the key exchange.
slots.deliverable: A written conclusion stating the pair fails to exceed the classical bound of 2, plus the QKD red-flag explanation.

slots.practicalActivity: Run the lab's own closing problem: take (|00⟩−|01⟩−|10⟩+|11⟩)/2, set up the full product-state ansatz, match all four coefficients, and determine whether a consistent solution for a,b,c,d exists or whether you hit a contradiction, stating your final verdict.
slots.deliverable: The full coefficient-matching work and a final entangled/product-state verdict with the specific values or contradiction shown.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short explanation, in your own words, of why the mismatch between the cloning unitary's actual output on |+⟩ (an entangled Bell state) and the required output (|+⟩⊗|+⟩) is what proves no-cloning, specifically explaining why the argument depends on U being linear.
slots.deliverable: A written explanation naming the specific mismatch (Bell state vs. clean product state) and why linearity is the load-bearing assumption in the proof.

lessons.title: Why No-Cloning Matters for Computing & Security

slots.practicalActivity: Write a precise explanation, citing the no-cloning theorem specifically (not just 'measurement disturbs things'), of why an eavesdropper intercepting a QKD channel cannot both learn the transmitted bit and pass an undisturbed copy onward to the receiver.
slots.deliverable: A written explanation that explicitly invokes no-cloning, rather than only measurement disturbance, to justify why eavesdropping is detectable.

slots.practicalActivity: Work through the Φ− branch of the teleportation protocol by hand: starting from Bob's qubit at (0.6,−0.8), apply the Z correction and confirm it yields exactly (0.6,0.8), then write a short explanation of why Bob cannot skip waiting for Alice's classical message.
slots.deliverable: The hand-worked Z-correction calculation confirming (0.6,0.8), plus a written explanation of why Bob needs Alice's classical bits.

slots.practicalActivity: Work through why Bob's single Bell measurement can distinguish the '10' message's result (|Φ−⟩) from the '00' message's result (|Φ+⟩) with certainty, explicitly tying your explanation to the mutual-orthogonality property of the four Bell states.
slots.deliverable: A written explanation connecting Bob's perfect distinguishability to the mutual orthogonality of |Φ+⟩ and |Φ−⟩ specifically.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a paragraph explaining why the Schrödinger equation's linearity is specifically what guarantees a qubit in superposition doesn't spontaneously collapse just from evolving in time, and why measurement must therefore be treated as a genuinely separate kind of process.
slots.deliverable: A written paragraph connecting linearity to superposition-preservation and distinguishing ordinary evolution from measurement.

slots.practicalActivity: Using U(t)=diag(e^(−iπ/4), e^(iπ/4)), compute by hand what happens when it's applied to |0⟩ versus |+⟩, confirming |0⟩ picks up only a global phase while |+⟩ develops an observable relative phase, and explain in writing why the same matrix produces such different observable effects on the two inputs.
slots.deliverable: Both hand computations (U(t)|0⟩ and U(t)|+⟩) and a written explanation of why one effect is global (invisible) and the other relative (physical).

slots.practicalActivity: Explain in writing, using H=(ħω/2)Z, why |0⟩ (an energy eigenstate) keeps the exact same measurement probabilities forever under time evolution while |+⟩ (not an energy eigenstate) develops an observable relative phase, tying the difference specifically to |+⟩ being a superposition of the two different-energy eigenstates.
slots.deliverable: A written explanation citing the energy-eigenstate property of |0⟩ and |1⟩ versus |+⟩'s mixed-energy composition as the source of the difference.

lessons.title: Why Quantum Gates Are Time Evolution

slots.practicalActivity: Write an explanation connecting classical AND/OR gate irreversibility to quantum gate reversibility, specifically tracing the difference back to the unitarity requirement (U†U=I) and what it would mean physically for a hypothetical non-unitary 'gate' to not correspond to valid time evolution.
slots.deliverable: A written explanation that ties AND/OR irreversibility versus quantum gate reversibility directly to the U†U=I requirement.

slots.practicalActivity: Work the lab's own closing problem: for M=[[1,1],[0,1]] proposed as a quantum gate, state what property you'd need to check (without fully computing M†M) and explain in writing what it would mean physically if M failed that check.
slots.deliverable: A written statement naming the unitarity check needed and the physical meaning (probability not conserved, invalid time evolution) if M fails it.

slots.practicalActivity: Work the lesson's own closing problem: |ψ⟩=0.6|0⟩+0.8|1⟩ is measured and the outcome is 0 (probability 0.36). State the qubit's exact state and measurement probabilities immediately afterward, and explain in writing how this differs from just saying 'there was a 36% chance of this.'
slots.deliverable: The post-measurement state (|0⟩, P(0)=1, P(1)=0) and a written explanation distinguishing the pre-measurement probability from the post-measurement certainty.

slots.practicalActivity: Work the lesson's own closing problem: apply CNOT (qubit 1 control, qubit 2 target) to |00⟩ directly, without first applying Hadamard, and determine using the factoring test whether the result is entangled or a product state.
slots.deliverable: The CNOT-on-|00⟩ result (unchanged, |00⟩) and the factoring-test work showing it is a trivial product state, not entangled.

lessons.title: Capstone: Explaining Quantum Mechanics to a Software Engineer

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own full response to the capstone's closing scenario: a colleague claims 'quantum advantage just comes from having more qubits, like more classical bits.' Using at least two of interference, entanglement, and no-cloning, write a clear, accurate rebuttal explaining what makes quantum computing structurally different, as if explaining it to a skilled software engineer with no physics background.
slots.deliverable: A written rebuttal essay, citing at least two of interference, entanglement, and no-cloning, explaining why qubit count alone doesn't capture quantum computing's structural advantage.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can reason precisely about qubits, superposition, measurement, entanglement, no-cloning, and unitary time evolution as physics rather than just formulas — able to prove a state is entangled by the factoring test, walk through Born-rule probabilities and collapse, trace teleportation and superdense coding protocols by hand, and explain to a fellow engineer exactly why quantum computing is structurally different from adding more classical bits.
